requirements.evidence: app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:71-85 appends "\n<@id>" on its own line and reserves room (MaxContentLength - mb_strlen($suffix)) so the mention survives truncation; no-mention path unchanged (`return mb_substr($base, 0, self::MaxContentLength)`). mentionId() at :91-118 trims strings, accepts ints, rejects bools/others, and validates `/^[0-9]{17,20}$/` after trim, so `@everyone`, `123`, `"123\n@everyone"` are rejected. config/services.php:40 adds `mention_id`, .env.example:79 adds `DISCORD_MENTION_ID=`, docs updated. Functionally complete; minor concern: float branch (:102-106) can emit a wrong ID due to precision loss.

security.evidence: Strict anchored snowflake regex `/^[0-9]{17,20}$/` applied after trim (app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:113) blocks @everyone/@here and newline injection; invalid values silently yield null. Webhook URL handling and redaction untouched.

readability.evidence: Clear names (`mentionId`, `$suffix`, `$available`), PHPDoc on the helper, consistent with the private-helper style of the class (`safe()`).

issues.explanation: New behavior (mention append, snowflake validation incl. @everyone/newline cases, truncation preserving the mention) ships without any Pest/PHPUnit test, violating the project's mandatory TDD convention.
Float values are accepted and formatted with sprintf('%.0f'), but floats cannot represent 17-20 digit IDs exactly, so this branch can ping a wrong user; it should be rejected rather than converted.
The `$available < 0` clamp is unreachable given MaxContentLength 1800 and a mention of at most 24 characters.
The new entry is followed by a blank line, splitting the 'Added' list in two.

review.summary: The change adds an optional DISCORD_MENTION_ID setting, strictly validates it as a 17-20 digit snowflake, and appends `<@id>` on its own line while reserving room so the mention survives truncation; config, .env.example, ops docs and CHANGELOG are updated. The implementation is correct and safe, but it ships with no tests at all despite the project's mandatory test-first convention, and includes a dubious float-conversion branch, so it needs changes before merging.
